abstract: Presale property inspection relied on a manual and paper based process in which sales agents prepared documentation, inspected each field of a unit by hand, recorded issues, and wrote an inspection report afterwards. This project built a web application that partially automates that process with Autodesk cloud products. The system imports Revit models from the Autodesk BIM 360 document system through the Forge API, extracts the property fields to be checked, and lets an administrator assign models to sales agents who then run guided inspections. Issues found during an inspection are created with attached photos and committed back to BIM 360, and the system automatically generates a PDF report that is emailed to the customer and the sales agent. The application was developed in PHP 7 with the Yii 2 framework, uses MariaDB, and was deployed to a live web server.

aliases: Task and Resource Tracking System for Agile Software Development Teams
abstract: Software companies usually work on multiple projects by using more than one teams. Most of the time, members in these teams could be assigned to several projects concurrently. This project aims to implement a system called 'Trax' which is integrated to an existing task repository system. It allows team members to input their daily scrum report. Team leads are able to monitor their agile team progresses on a day-to-day basis while the top management could track the resource usages by individual projects, personnels, and teams.

abstract: ISL members have been using Scrum Methodology for software development. Sometimes, using just Excel files to keep track of things going on, who is doing what tasks, who has effort left to do incoming tasks, and what the status of the task is in right now, in each sprint is a painful thing and there is no tools to aid them. So, we decided to find a way and develop one thing that can help them, which is Task Assistant, planning and keeping track of things in an efficient way. Also, we foresee that daily task planning is useful for personal use. So, we provided not only team assistance but also personal assistance to aid all types of users.

canonical_title: Radio Frequency Identification for Counting Lap-Based Running
abstract: Fit for Run activity is a daily running activity, which needed several staffs and take a long time to pay attention in operation. Lap counting, and summarization of runners were operated by staffs manually. In traditional solution, several hours are required for giving a plastic brand for a lap then summarize those runners' records into papers at the end of the day. Moreover, all those records could not deliver to runners instantly. Our project brought some technologies to solve the problems using a combination of technologies. Normally, this kind of event is usually a small local community event, which only has little budget and manpower that could be allocated in the management of the event. Therefore, expenditure should be primary sector that we need to concern about it. Also, its specification should be sufficient to improve the operation of this event. Due to the lack of cost-effective solution for the problem domain, this study proposes a cost-effective interactive platform that is based on low-frequency (LF) RFID devices instead of using ultra-high frequency (UHF) RFID because their costs are totally different. The proposed platforms help manage the running events, log runner specifics, manages data through a centralized database, and show participants' data such as lap counting and result in real time. The proposed system web application was deployed on cloud web server including database server and been used at the Fit for Run Event at Assumption University on 1-22 February 2017.
